well: EPICA Dome C 1999 (EDC99) ice borehole - EAST ANTARCTIC PLATEAU (75.10 S, 123.35 E; surface elevation +3,233 m, the highest site in the catalogue), Dome C, one of the coldest and driest places on Earth; the lowest ~164 m of the 3,270 m core (3026.58-3190.08 m depth), holding the OLDEST ice ever recovered at publication: 611-799 kyr BP on the EDC3 gas timescale
operator_on_log: University of Bern (Physics Institute, Climate and Environmental Physics) - Luethi, Le Floch, Bereiter, Blunier, Barnola, Siegenthaler, Raynaud, Jouzel, Fischer, Kawamura, Stocker; drilling by the European Project for Ice Coring in Antarctica (EPICA), EU FP4/FP5 funded (grant IDs in header)
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.710901 ('CO2 record from the EPICA Dome C 1999 (EDC99) ice core covering 650 to 800 kyr BP measured at the University of Bern'); supplement to Luethi et al. 2008, Nature 453, 379-382 (doi:10.1038/nature06949) - the paper that extended humanity's direct record of the ancient atmosphere from 650,000 to 800,000 years
license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (CC-BY-3.0), declared IN the file's own header and license-checked BEFORE cataloguing. Attribution: Luethi et al. / PANGAEA / EPICA
fetch_method: read-only HTTPS fetch of the PANGAEA textfile export - COMPLETE dataset (741 data points per the header's own Size declaration, re-counted EXACT at gate time: 247 rows x 3 counted columns with the depth geocode excluded) in one fetch, closing at the declared MAXIMUM DEPTH 3190.08 m to the last row
coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 247 trapped-gas measurements (means of 1237 individual samples per the header comment) - depth 3026.58-3190.08 m, gas age 611.269-798.512 ka BP (EDC3), CO2 171.6-260.3 ppmv with per-measurement standard deviations 0.2-3.7
curves: CO2 [ppmv] 171.6-260.3 - the trapped ancient atmosphere itself
source_anomaly_disclosure: Preserved as published, with two honest disclosures: (1) the header's own comment reports measurements 'at 289 depth intervals' while this table archives 247 - the remaining intervals ride in the companion PANGAEA datasets of the same publication (LGGE Grenoble record doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.710903 and the collection doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.710936); the Size declaration describes THIS table and closes EXACT at 741; (2) the wider community record: Bereiter et al. 2015 (GRL) later identified an analytical bias in portions of the original 2008 measurements and issued a revised CO2 composite - this entry archives the ORIGINAL Nature-2008 dataset exactly as PANGAEA serves it, bias and all, because the catalogue preserves archives, it does not repair them; noted also: ages are in ka BP so 798.512 ka = ~0.8 Ma, and the deep ice is glaciologically thinned - the record's 163.5 m span covers 187.2 kyr (mean 87.3 cm ice per kyr)
purpose: FIFTIETH catalogue entry - the milestone - and the catalogue's boldest possible answer to 'what can a well hold': ANCIENT AIR. The East Antarctic Plateau joins as region THIRTY-SEVEN (Dome C, +3,233 m - the highest site in the catalogue, its third cryosphere borehole after GISP2 and Agassiz but its first ANTARCTIC ice) and ice-core trapped gas is kind THIRTY-NINE - not rock, not fluid, not a log: bubbles of the actual atmosphere of 611,000-799,000 years ago, sealed as firn closed and carried down 3 km of ice, including the LOWEST atmospheric CO2 ever directly measured (171.6 ppmv at 667.6 ka, re-derived at every gate run) and the two 'lukewarm interglacials' whose CO2 never reached 260.3 ppmv - every one of the 247 archived values of the ancient atmosphere sits BELOW the preindustrial 280, a fact the gate re-proves on every run
verified: 247 rows / 741 counted cells against the header's own Size declaration (EXACT, depth geocode excluded); depth AND gas age both strictly monotonic across all 247 rows; depth min/max match the header Coverage declarations EXACT (3026.58 / 3190.08); CO2 min 171.6 ppmv at 667.569 ka and max 260.3 ppmv at 786.587 ka pinned; all 247 CO2 values < 280 ppmv preindustrial pinned; std-dev envelope 0.2-3.7 pinned; 289-vs-247 interval disclosure and Bereiter-2015 revision disclosure pinned; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
